title: Sort by the last digit first?
hook: Three passes, three digits. Which order works?

knows: stable sorting: ties keep their order
doesNotKnow: that sorting by the least important digit first works
that each later pass decides the order and stability keeps the earlier passes' work

misconception: To sort numbers digit by digit you must start with the first (biggest) digit.
objective: The learner can explain that radix sort deals by the last digit first, then the middle, then the first, and that because each pass keeps ties in order the most important digit has the last word, so three passes sort any list of three-digit numbers.

claims.text: Sorting 329 457 657 839 436 720 355 by the last digit, then the middle digit, then the first digit, keeping ties in their current order, ends fully sorted: 329 355 436 457 657 720 839.
claims.source: Builder's node script (scratchpad verify.mjs): three stable bucket passes in order of place 0, 1, 2 give 720 355 436 457 657 329 839, then 720 329 436 839 355 457 657, then 329 355 436 457 657 720 839, equal to the sorted list. Also agrees with sort on 20,000 random lists of 2-13 three-digit numbers. | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-14 (pass 19): Own stable bucket passes (scratchpad fc19b2/radix.mjs): 720 355 436 457 657 329 839 -> 720 329 436 839 355 457 657 -> 329 355 436 457 657 720 839 = sorted.

claims.text: Doing the same passes first digit to last (first digit, then middle, then last) ends 720 355 436 457 657 329 839, which is ordered by the last digit only; the first digit went first, so the later passes overwrote its work.
claims.source: Builder's node script: passes of place 2, 1, 0 give 329 355 457 436 657 720 839, then 329 720 436 839 355 457 657, then 720 355 436 457 657 329 839. The reveal says 'ordered by the last digit only' and the final pass is by last digit; the list is not sorted. | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-14 (pass 19): Own run places 2,1,0: 329 355 457 436 657 720 839 -> 329 720 436 839 355 457 657 -> 720 355 436 457 657 329 839; last digits 0 5 6 7 7 9 9 ascending, list not sorted (436 after 355 fine but 329 after 657). Reveal branch in Demo.tsx shows this text only when not sorted. | v3 2026-10-14 (demo-builder): the first-digit-first run is now its own row of pass buttons and the gate requires finishing it, so the reveal quotes a run the learner did. Second clause reworded. Reopened.

claims.text: On pass 3 of last digit first, the cards in the ringed bucket tied on the first digit and kept the order the earlier passes had given them, so the earlier digits settle ties and the first digit, dealt last, has the last word. The stage caption reads 'Tie in bucket N: kept the order earlier passes gave it'.
claims.source: Stable pass: bucket contents keep list order (bucket 7 after the first pass holds 457 then 657, as in the input). Radix sort correctness needs each pass stable: CLRS 4th ed. section 8.3 (Lemma 8.3 in the 3rd ed.), whose Figure 8.3 uses this input. | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-14 (pass 19): Derivation: Demo.tsx deal() pushes in list order into each bucket and flattens buckets 0-9, so equal-digit cards keep prior order (stable). Inductively after pass p the list is sorted on the last p digits. CLRS 4e 8.3 / Figure 8.3 (this input) from memory, not opened; argument re-derived. | v3 2026-10-14 (demo-builder): the stage now rings the first bucket holding two or more cards on a third pass (bucket 3: 329 then 355 for last-first; bucket 7: 457 then 657 for first-first) with that caption. Reopened.

claims.text: Three passes sort three-digit numbers however many there are.
claims.source: CLRS section 8.3: radix sort of n numbers with d digits makes d passes, each a stable sort (time Theta(d(n + k))). Here d = 3. Builder's random check in node over 20,000 lists of 2-13 numbers. | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-14 (pass 19): Same induction as c3 with d = 3 places; own random check: 50,000 lists of 1-40 three-digit numbers incl. duplicates, three passes always equal numeric sort.

claims.text: The stage marks each neighbouring pair with < when it is in order and > when it is not.
claims.source: Comparison of adjacent values in the collected list, computed in Demo.tsx; for the pass-2 list 720 329 436 839 355 457 657 the marks are > < < > < <. | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-14 (pass 19): Demo.tsx: mark is '<' iff v < next, else '>'; values distinct so no equal case. Own run of pass-2 list gives > < < > < <.

recall.question: Radix sort deals 3-digit numbers into buckets one digit at a time, keeping ties in order. Which digit should the LAST pass use?
options: Any digit; the order does not matter
recall.why: The last pass has the last word. Earlier passes survive only as the order of ties, so the most important digit goes last.
